entries.title: Document for humans and machines
entries.summary: The user requires persistent repository memory readable by any AI provider, with human-readable and machine-readable documentation kept current together.
details: Maintain MEMORY.md and MEMORY.json together as knowledge changes; a chat transcript or provider-private memory is insufficient.
For behavior or interface changes, also maintain the relevant human guides and existing machine contracts.

entries.title: Mac Control architecture and documentation
entries.summary: Mac Control is a self-hosted macOS dashboard for controls, cooling, USB storage, and system activity.
details: The server uses the Python standard library; native helpers use Objective-C and macOS frameworks; the frontend uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
README.md describes user-facing behavior; docs/REFERENCE.md covers implementation and maintenance; docs/machines/mbp15.md is the machine runbook.
docs/API.md covers the full Mac Control HTTP API; packages/contracts/README.md identifies local API contracts and the separate Notifier exports.
DevBox Notifier is a separate optional service. Its integration guide is docs/integrations/mac-control.md; machine contracts live in packages/contracts/.

entries.title: Mac Control HTTP interface
entries.summary: Mac Control's full HTTP API and the first integration use case are documented in docs/API.md, packages/contracts/mac-control.openapi.json and packages/contracts/mac-control-api.json.
details: The implementation has 32 GET/POST operations under /api/. Documentation revision is 1.5.0; there is no negotiated API version. Authenticated /api/openapi.json serves the full contract with its bridge reference; /api/ui serves the UI map; /api/docs serves both Markdown guides. Hardware schemas remain extensible.

Requests require private/loopback/link-local source and known Host/port checks; cross-site fetches are rejected. POST requires exact http://Host Origin for direct access or the configured HTTPS origin for trusted loopback Tailscale Serve, and a JSON object from 1 through 4096 bytes, even for login and logout.

Private routes use the mac_control cookie, with fixed 24-hour normal or 30-day remembered expiry. Session inspection, sign-in, first setup and stats/leave do not require a valid session; setup requires loopback and leave can remove only the supplied cookie/viewer lease. There is no Mac Control bearer-token API.

Maintain docs/API.md, docs/UI.md, the local OpenAPI, API/use-case manifest, dashboard-ui.json and both memory files together as behavior changes. packages/contracts/openapi.json is the separate Notifier API.

entries.title: First API integration: Notifier copy progress
entries.summary: The user identified DevBox Notifier copy progress as the first API integration use case; this does not establish a historical deployment date.
details: The browser polls GET /api/file-activity with its Mac Control session. After authorization, the server pulls GET /v1/snapshot over fixed loopback using a private administrator bearer from configured state_dir/admin-token. Notifier does not POST activity into Mac Control; notifications/streaming are separate.

The bridge uses a two-second timeout, a 2 MiB response cap and no environment proxies. Caught upstream/configuration failures return HTTP 200 available=false with empty activity lists; this is not evidence that no copy is running.

Each visible authenticated client waits two seconds after request completion before polling again. The local UI shows up to eight qualifying active copies, overall progress and a current filename summary; unavailable/error responses hide the section. English operation/measured-detail filters can omit localized Finder observations. Window disappearance does not prove completion.

The separate Notifier repository owns the five exported version 1.1.0 activity contracts (2026-11-01). Local API/use-case documents describe this checkout; reading them is not a live check of the separate Notifier service.

entries.title: This checkout is the live installation
entries.summary: The execution machine is mbp15, and this checkout is its live Mac Control installation according to the machine runbook.
details: The checkout is /Users/paolo/personal/mac-control. The user launch agent is ~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.maccontrol.server.plist, label local.maccontrol.server; the dashboard uses port 8765.
Before managing the service, run python3 service.py status to verify the active location. Do not start a second server on port 8765 or move/remove the checkout while the launch agent points here.

Frontend changes are live. Python changes require a dashboard restart; native changes use the installer. Dashboard management does not require restarting privileged fan or input helpers. An input-helper restart resets both built-in inputs to On.
The old ~/Library/Application Support/Mac Control/.runtime compatibility symlink must remain for existing permission and notifier paths.

entries.title: Preserve private runtime and backups
entries.summary: Runtime state and migration backups are private, untracked local data that must be preserved.
details: .runtime/ contains credentials, sessions, settings, compiled helpers, and logs. .local-backups/ contains private migration backups.
Never commit, upload, copy into memory, or replace these directories with fixtures or another installation's state.
Preserve saved state and the existing compatibility symlink during updates.

entries.title: Match checks to the change
entries.summary: Use the repository's documented checks when relevant; recording a command here does not mean it has been run.
details: The Python test suite is python3 -m unittest discover.
Native build preflight is ./install.command --check.
Check the active installation with python3 service.py status before service management. Documentation-only work needs no service restart.

entries.title: Read-only host battery and Tailscale indicators
entries.summary: The dashboard has a compact host battery gauge and Tailscale status strip above System activity.
details: GET /api/host-status requires a session and returns battery and Tailscale summaries from read-only local commands, plus Claude and Codex quota summaries (see their usage-indicator entries); no peer or account data.

Reads use two-second command timeouts and a shared ten-second demand-driven cache. The visible authenticated browser polls ten seconds after completion; hidden, signed-out and unloaded pages pause polling.

Tailscale connected requires BackendState=Running and Self.Online=true. Missing CLI, login/approval needs, disconnected and unavailable states are explicit; unknown battery readings do not become zero.

entries.title: Claude plan usage pill from the Claude Code status line
entries.summary: A pill beside the Auto/Intel/AMD graphics toggle shows Claude plan 5-hour, weekly and Fable weekly usage reported by Claude Code.
details: Decision (2026-11-03): Mac Control never reads Claude credentials or contacts Anthropic itself; Claude Code supplies all usage data with its own sign-in.

Sources: (1) Claude Code's statusLine runs claude_usage.py after each reply (stdin rate_limits has only five_hour/seven_day/spend_limit, no Fable). (2) While host status is requested, UsageProbe runs the claude CLI's experimental get_usage control request (no prompt, no model call, no saved session) at most every 5 minutes; it adds per-model weekly windows (model_scoped, e.g. Fable) and fresh 5h/7d including claude.ai usage.

Both write only usage windows to .runtime/claude-usage.json (0600, atomic, flock); spend/credits/account details are discarded. Merge: reports within one hour of the same resets_at keep the highest usage; a later window replaces an earlier one; a reply without per-model data keeps the stored list.

/api/host-status returns claude.state available/not-configured/unavailable, fiveHour/sevenDay (null after resetsAt) and modelWeekly (expired omitted). The UI dims readings older than 30 minutes, hides Fable unless reported, and shows Manila reset times in the tooltip.

On mbp15 (2026-11-03): the user configured the statusLine; the claude Team plan provides rate_limits; the usage check was verified working under the launch agent. The statusLine command path must change if the checkout moves.

The 5-hour window shows a local Resets in H:MM:SS countdown from resetsAt, refreshed each second while visible and signed in without extra requests. Missing/expired windows hide the timer; at zero the old percentage clears to — until fresh usage arrives.

entries.title: Stable mobile tabs and chart inspection
entries.summary: Mobile section buttons preserve their screen position, and charts support sample inspection.
details: Mobile uses sticky tabs, content-sized panes and a viewport-sized minimum workspace; tab focus and section switching preserve scroll position. USB cards retain DOM identity across polls.

Overview, expanded and daily energy charts support mouse hover, tap and keyboard inspection with Manila time and units. Values come from recorded samples; missing samples are not interpolated. Expand icons have separate 44px targets.

entries.title: Separate password unlock from normal mounting
entries.summary: Encrypted-drive mounting requests passwords only for locked targets and preserves mount errors for unlocked targets.
details: Unlock actions request mounted=true even for partially mounted drives. Password submissions explicitly request Mount; older in-flight polls cannot overwrite an action result.

The Python manager invokes native unlock only when fresh metadata reports a locked target. Native already-unlocked targets return the normal mount result directly; requiresPassword is reserved for targets still locked.

Unlock diagnostics use fixed authentication, privacy (TCC), permission or general messages in the API, without raw command output. On failure the helper writes diskutil's stderr (never the password) to its stderr, which drives.py logs to .runtime/server.log. Passwords remain stdin-only and are never saved.

diskutil error -69464 ('restricted by sandbox') is a TCC Removable Volumes denial; the background service cannot show the consent prompt, so Terminal unlocks succeed while the dashboard fails. TCC attributes requests to the launch agent's first executable, so the agent runs the Command Line Tools Python.app binary directly (identifier com.apple.python3), not caffeinate or the /usr/bin/python3 shim, and server.py starts `caffeinate -is -w <pid>` when MAC_CONTROL_STAY_AWAKE=1. On mbp15 that Python.app has Full Disk Access (granted 2026-11-03). Disk-image volumes are not subject to this check, so test images do not reproduce it.

entries.title: Codex plan usage beside Claude
entries.summary: A matching pill beside Claude shows Codex quota percentages used, actual window durations and Manila reset times.
details: Host-status cache refresh triggers a shared background codex app-server account/rateLimits/read check at most every five minutes (30-second timeout, 1 MiB output cap, never concurrent). No prompt, thread or model turn is created.

Codex manages its own ChatGPT sign-in; Mac Control never reads Codex credentials or sends direct OpenAI HTTP requests. Only the codex bucket primary/secondary quota windows are retained, in memory; raw account, credit and other bucket details are discarded.

/api/host-status returns codex.state available/checking/not-configured/unavailable, updatedAt and nullable primary/secondary {usedPercent, resetsAt, windowMinutes}. Failures retain the last good reading with its original timestamp; expired windows become null. Restart clears the cache. UI dims readings older than 30 minutes.

CLI discovery supports PATH, Codex/ChatGPT app bundles, ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin and /usr/local/bin. On mbp15, the ChatGPT bundled CLI returned 5-hour and weekly limits on 2026-11-03. Only the dashboard needs restarting for Python changes.
Claude and Codex stay together in a flex group; quota windows stack at laptop widths and on mobile, with both provider names visible.

Reported 300-minute windows show a local Resets in H:MM:SS countdown from resetsAt, refreshed each second while visible and signed in without extra requests. Missing/expired windows hide the timer; at zero the old percentage clears to — until fresh usage arrives.

entries.title: Private HTTPS publication at /mc
entries.summary: On mbp15, Mac Control is published privately at https://mbp15.tail19753.ts.net/mc through persistent Tailscale Serve.
details: The /mc Serve mount proxies to the existing 127.0.0.1:8765 dashboard. Existing / (8080), /tmb (8877) and HTTPS 8443 (8876) routes are preserved; Funnel is not enabled.
Optional .runtime/tailscale-serve.json (0600) specifies exact lowercase HTTPS ts.net origin and path_prefix; read at startup with a 4096-byte cap. Invalid configuration fails startup.

Forwarded requests require a loopback TCP peer, exact configured Host and X-Forwarded-Host, and X-Forwarded-Proto=https. Untrusted forwarding and Funnel-marked requests are rejected; POST Origin must match the configured HTTPS origin.

The existing dashboard password and session checks remain required. Serve never grants localhost-only first setup or helper-path access. HTTPS cookies use Secure and the prefix scope (/mc/); direct local/LAN cookies retain Path=/. Serve sign-in failures share the proxy loopback rate-limit bucket.

Serve strips the mount; server HTML links/meta and browser fetches preserve the prefix externally. Publish with tailscale serve --bg --https=443 --set-path=/mc http://127.0.0.1:8765; remove only this route with tailscale serve --https=443 --set-path=/mc off. Python/config changes need only a dashboard restart.

entries.title: Complete dashboard data/actions and in-app guide
entries.summary: All dashboard hardware controls and presets have JSON action APIs; graphs and indicators expose read-only numeric data. A ? beside Connected locally opens the repository design/UI and API guides.
details: GET /api/fans and /api/graphics read helper/policy state without leasing telemetry. GET /api/stats/history returns existing two-minute samples without creating or renewing a viewer lease; live clients still use /api/stats?viewer=ID and stats/leave.

GET /api/power/samples?hours=1|12|24 returns unbucketed stored time/watts/connected/day/cumulative_wh readings under the monitor lock, preserving nulls and gaps. Detail retention is 24 hours; existing /api/power supplies chart histories and 90-day totals/coverage.

web/presets.json is the shared named-preset catalog. GET /api/presets reads it and POST /api/presets applies supported controls sequentially. Application can partially succeed; inspect applied/skipped/state/error and re-read after a helper/transport failure. The browser uses the same endpoint.

GET /api/docs returns docs/UI.md and docs/API.md as Markdown; web/guide.js renders text nodes, headings, tables, lists and code in a native modal. The ? has a hover title and stays visible on mobile. Live docs/contracts require the existing session/network checks and preserve the Tailscale prefix.

packages/contracts/dashboard-ui.json maps each element and graph to usage, fields, units and read/action APIs. Browser tabs, chart ranges/cursors, expansion and drafts remain local presentation state; clients build their own views. No write API alters historical observations or exposes private runtime files.

entries.title: Wait for bootout before bootstrapping helpers
entries.summary: The fan, input and graphics helper installers must wait for launchd to remove the old job before bootstrapping the new one.
details: launchctl bootout is asynchronous. On mbp15 (2026-11-05) the fan helper took about 0.8 s to exit, and an immediate bootstrap failed with "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error" (launchd: "37: Operation already in progress"), leaving no helper loaded and fans in Apple Auto.
Each installer polls launchctl print system/<label> for up to 30 s after bootout and exits with a rerun message if the job remains. test_installer.py checks the bootout -> wait -> bootstrap order.

If the fan helper is not running when its installer starts, the installer restores the dashboard's saved selection (.runtime/fan-settings.json) instead of the hardware's Apple Auto state. The dashboard itself restores fan mode only during its own startup.
